title: Building an offer that justifies a higher rate for Pet grooming
audience: Pet groomers, including mobile groomers, who want to move from a single price per dog to clear grooming packages.
learningOutcomes: Write an offer with a clear promised outcome, time frame and conditions
Identify the friction and risk the customer carries and reduce them
Price the offer on value and cost, not only time

instruction.heading: A bad offer versus a good offer
instruction.body: 'I can groom your dog' is a service. 'A full clip for your medium dog, with a bath, a tidy, teeth brushing if you want it, a photo of the result at pick-up, and a free touch-up within a set window if matting shows up a few days later' is an offer. The owner buys the result, the certainty of getting it and the time saved. A groomer who quotes one price per dog is compared on that price alone, and the owner cannot see what makes the groom worth more.

instruction.heading: The five parts of a grooming offer
instruction.body: Name the outcome: a clean, comfortable coat cut to the agreed style. Set the time frame: the drop-off, the pick-up and the booking length. List what the owner must do: give health notes and any medication, and brush out a coat that is heavily matted before the visit if they can. Add one certainty element, such as a photo at pick-up. State the risk you carry, such as what you will do if a dog is not fit to groom, within your insurance. Put the scope and exclusions in writing, because a written quote can become binding once it is accepted (business.gov.au, 1 August 2025).

instruction.heading: Packages that step up
instruction.body: Groomers commonly sell a wash and dry, a full clip, and a full clip with add-ons. Airtasker's vendor guide lists a medium-dog wash and dry at $45 to $50, and a medium full clip at $85 to $100 (last updated 17 March 2025). Hepper, another vendor, lists a medium full summer cut at $90 (updated 5 January 2026). Use both only to show the spread, and do not average them. Add-ons can be separate lines on the quote: Airtasker lists teeth brushing at $10 and flea and tick treatment at $10 to $20 (17 March 2025). Jobber describes stepped packages in which each higher level adds something the customer can see (updated 8 October 2024).

instruction.heading: Guarantees, claims and the total
instruction.body: Consumer guarantees under the Australian Consumer Law apply to services and cannot be removed by contract. Do not claim that a clip reduces skin problems or shedding by a percentage unless you have measured it. Show one total and say whether GST applies, as Western Australia's consumer agency asks (WA Consumer Protection, 4 September 2026). A workmanship promise you choose to add sits on top of the consumer guarantees (business.gov.au, 27 May 2025). Under the consumer guarantees, a business should be given a reasonable chance to fix a minor fault free of charge, so a stated fix-first policy is both a promise and consistent with that rule (Consumer Victoria, 13 October 2023).

instruction.heading: Price on value, then check cost
instruction.body: Price from the outcome and the risk, check against your cost and time, and then decide on any premium. Government guidance says a quote should recover every cost and add a margin (business.gov.au, 1 August 2025). Grooming rules differ by place. NSW has a code of practice for pet grooming establishments, whose mandatory status is not confirmed in the research. The ACT's code says its principles also apply to grooming at clients' homes. The research did not find a Victorian grooming code, which is not the same as finding that no rule applies, so Victorian grooming rules remain UNRESOLVED. Check the rule for your state before you describe a mobile service.

procedure: Write the outcome in one sentence an owner would repeat, such as a clean coat cut to the agreed style, ready at pick-up.
Set the booking length and the pick-up time, and check them against your record of time for each dog size.
List what the owner must provide, such as health notes and medication, and reduce each step.
Add one certainty element, such as a photo at pick-up.
Set the packages and their add-on lines, and check each add-on price against your costs.
Price from value, check against cost and time, and state one total with GST status.

workedExamples.situation: A groomer in Victoria quotes one price for a medium dog, $60 for a bath and tidy and $95 for a full clip, which is an illustrative quote. Owners compare it with listings and she loses a regular client to a cheaper listing. The client's dog needs a full clip and teeth brushing every six weeks, and the quote does not show teeth brushing separately.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Rewrite the offer as three levels and set the add-on lines. What does the offer say about a dog that is not fit to groom?
workedExamples.reasoning: She writes three levels: wash and dry; full clip; and full clip with teeth brushing and a photo at pick-up. Airtasker's vendor range for a medium full clip is $85 to $100 (17 March 2025), and Hepper lists a medium full summer cut at $90 (5 January 2026). She places her own price inside her costs and does not average the two sources. Teeth brushing is a separate line, which Airtasker lists at $10. She states that she will not groom a dog that shows signs of illness or parasites, and tells the owner at drop-off. The NSW code, where it applies, says animals with suspected infectious disease must not be admitted. Her offer promises only what she can deliver.

equipmentAndPpe: Written offer with three levels and add-on lines
Price list showing cost by dog size
Written health-notes form for owners, dated

commonErrors.error: Quoting one price per dog with no outcome, so the owner compares on price alone
commonErrors.prevention: Write the outcome, the time and the photo into the offer.

commonErrors.error: Making a guarantee you cannot afford, such as an open-ended free re-groom
commonErrors.prevention: Limit any free touch-up to a stated window and to a fault you control.

commonErrors.error: Stating a result you cannot substantiate, such as fewer skin problems
commonErrors.prevention: Use only results you have recorded.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Business guidance only. This lesson does not grant any licence, registration or authority to run a grooming business or a mobile grooming service.

NSW: Animal Welfare Code of Practice No 8 covers pet grooming establishments and was originally published in October 1996. The research did not confirm whether it is mandatory today, and the code says it may be revised. Check its current status before relying on it.

ACT: the Code of Practice for Pet Grooming Establishments applies to grooming for fee, and its principles also apply to grooming in specially fitted vehicles and at clients' homes. The full PDF was not read for this research.

Victoria: no grooming code or registration requirement was found in the research. This does not show that no requirement applies. Victorian grooming rules are UNRESOLVED; check with the council or the state agency before describing a service.
The Australian Consumer Law applies to pricing statements, and misleading price statements are prohibited (ACCC, 15 July 2026).

qualityStandard: Each offer states the outcome, the time frame, the add-ons, the exclusions and one total price with GST status.
Each guarantee is one the groomer can deliver and that is limited to a stated window.
No result is claimed unless it has been recorded.
documentationEvidence: Written offer with three levels and add-on lines, dated
Price check showing cost, time and margin by dog size
Photo and health-notes record for each groom
summary: A good grooming offer promises a coat result, a time frame, a photo at pick-up and a guarantee you can keep.
Vendor prices differ between sources, so use them as a spread, not as your price.
Victorian grooming rules are unresolved, so check the rule for each place you groom before you describe a service.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which part of a grooming offer does the owner buy?
options: Your clippers and your brand of shampoo
How long you have been grooming

knowledgeChecks.question: What should a guarantee on a grooming offer be?
options: Unlimited, with no end date and no conditions
Impossible to claim on in any case
Only for owners who are your friends
Something you can deliver and afford

knowledgeChecks.question: What must a measurable claim, such as fewer skin problems after a clip, have?
options: A famous endorsement from a pet personality
A discount on the next groom
